paragraphs: Cybersecurity researcher. I break things to understand how to defend them - from AI-driven threats and blockchain security to network intrusion detection. Currently an M.Tech student at IIT Patna and a Junior Research Associate at the Cybersecurity Lab, building blockchain testbeds and poking at distributed systems.

I have multiple published papers (IEEE, Springer), multiple CTF wins and a habit of going down rabbit holes that sometimes turn into research. Looking for opportunities to do meaningful security research - the kind that makes systems actually safer, not just papers. If you have a project or research direction in mind, let's talk.

researchInterests.title: Research Focus
researchInterests.statement: My research interests focus on the security of distributed and blockchain systems. I am interested in understanding how these systems behave under realistic adversarial conditions and in exploring practical ways to evaluate and improve security, trust and reliability through experimentation and system-level analysis.
researchInterests.futureGoals: Adaptive with time. Currently looking forward to make cross-chain bridges more secure and to explore the security implications of AI in cybersecurity.

research.title: Beyond Copy-Pasting-Contextualizing LLMs for Secure Code Generation
research.description: This study evaluates security vulnerabilities in code generated by Large Language Models (LLMs) and copilots, emphasizing the need for strategic contextualization in secure coding practices. Through qualitative analysis, it assesses risks and proposes actionable strategies to help developers fine-tune LLMs for secure code generation. By integrating proactive security measures, this research aligns accelerated development with robust security practices.
research.tldr: LLM-generated code is riddled with vulnerabilities; strategic prompt contextualization can fix that.

research.title: Beyond Text: Nefarious Actors Harnessing LLMs for Strategic Advantage
research.description: This study explores how malicious actors exploit Large Language Models (LLMs) for cyber threats beyond conventional uses. Through literature review, case studies, and real-world analysis, it examines LLM-driven deception, social engineering, and cybercrimes such as phishing, password cracking, and malware propagation, highlighting emerging security challenges.
research.tldr: Bad actors are weaponizing LLMs for phishing, malware, and social engineering at scale.

research.title: Shadow APR-ing for APR Poisoning Detection
research.description: This study addresses ARP spoofing, a longstanding network security threat enabling attacks such as MITM and DDoS. It proposes an automated OS-based monitoring technique to detect ARP poisoning in real time, reducing reliance on manual ARP table checks and minimizing detection delays.
research.tldr: Automated OS-level ARP monitoring that catches poisoning attacks in real time without manual table checks.
